title: Spike — 14mo bearded dragon: tremors and a rubbery jaw
presentation: 14-month-old male bearded dragon, twitching in the hind limbs for a week, reluctant to walk, and the owner has noticed his lower jaw feels soft and his back legs look swollen.

stages.title: Assess the patient and the vivarium
stages.briefing: Weight 310 g. Hind-limb fasciculations, unwilling to bear weight, mandible pliable on gentle pressure, symmetrical firm swelling of both femora. Spine palpably irregular. Vivarium: UV tube in place but unchanged for 22 months, basking surface temperature 30°C (target 38–42°C), diet crickets and mealworms gut-loaded but never dusted, no calcium supplement, no direct sunlight.
stages.prompt: Which findings point to metabolic bone disease?

options.label: Pliable mandible with symmetrical femoral swelling
options.detail: Fibrous osteodystrophy of the long bones and jaw

options.label: Hind-limb tremors with reluctance to bear weight
options.detail: Hypocalcaemic neuromuscular signs

options.label: No calcium dusting and a UV tube 22 months old
options.detail: Both halves of the calcium pathway missing

options.label: Basking temperature 30°C
options.detail: Impairs digestion and appetite; not the direct cause of soft bone

options.label: Weight 310 g
options.detail: Within a normal range for the species

stages.explanation: A rubbery jaw with swollen femora and tremors is nutritional secondary hyperparathyroidism, and the vivarium supplies the mechanism twice over: no dietary calcium, and a UV tube that stopped emitting useful UVB about a year ago even though it still lights up. Owners reasonably assume a glowing tube is working, and it is worth saying so explicitly.

stages.title: Choose the tests
stages.briefing: The dragon is stable. You can take a small blood sample and radiograph.

options.label: Ionised calcium
options.detail: The fraction that determines the tremors

options.label: Total calcium and phosphorus with the Ca:P ratio
options.detail: Grades the imbalance

options.label: Whole-body radiographs
options.detail: Cortical thinning, folding fractures, spinal deformity

options.label: UV index measurement at the basking site with a UV meter
options.detail: Tests the lamp rather than trusting it

options.label: Uric acid and total protein
options.detail: Renal disease is the other cause of this biochemistry

options.label: Vitamin D3 assay as the only test
options.detail: Supportive, but slow, costly and not decisive on its own

options.label: Faecal parasitology before treating the hypocalcaemia
options.detail: Worth doing eventually; it does not change today

stages.explanation: The pairing that matters is ionised calcium with phosphorus, and the measurement that changes the household is the UV reading at the basking site: a meter turns advice into evidence. Uric acid is on the list because renal disease produces a similar picture and would change the treatment entirely.

stages.title: Interpret the results
stages.briefing: Ionised calcium 0.58 mmol/L (ref 1.2–1.6). Total calcium 1.9 mmol/L, phosphorus 3.4 mmol/L, Ca:P 0.56:1 (target 1.5–2:1). Uric acid 210 µmol/L (normal), total protein 52 g/L. Radiographs: generalised cortical thinning, bilateral folding fractures of the femora, kyphosis of the lumbar spine, no bladder or renal mineralisation. UV index at the basking site 0.1 (target 4–6). No renal enlargement on imaging.
stages.prompt: Which conclusions do these results support?

options.label: Nutritional secondary hyperparathyroidism with folding fractures
options.detail: Low ionised calcium, inverted Ca:P, thin cortices and folding fractures

options.label: The UV source is providing effectively no usable UVB
options.detail: A UV index of 0.1 against a target of 4–6

options.label: Renal secondary hyperparathyroidism is excluded
options.detail: Normal uric acid with no renal mineralisation or enlargement

options.label: Handling must be minimised because the bones will fracture
options.detail: Folding fractures already present

options.label: Hypovitaminosis A explains the presentation
options.detail: Causes squamous metaplasia and swollen eyelids, not soft bone

options.label: The tremors are a primary seizure disorder
options.detail: They are hypocalcaemic and will resolve as calcium is restored

stages.explanation: Distinguishing nutritional from renal secondary hyperparathyroidism is the intellectual work here, and the normal uric acid does it. The UV index of 0.1 is the most actionable number on the page. Recognising the folding fractures changes how the animal is handled from this minute — these are patients that break in the consulting room.

stages.title: Commit to a diagnosis
stages.briefing: Ionised calcium 0.58 mmol/L, Ca:P 0.56:1, cortical thinning with bilateral femoral folding fractures and kyphosis, normal uric acid, UV index 0.1 at the basking site, undusted insect diet.

options.label: Nutritional secondary hyperparathyroidism (metabolic bone disease) with pathological fractures
options.detail: The deficiency, its cause and its skeletal consequence

options.label: Renal secondary hyperparathyroidism
options.detail: Excluded by normal uric acid and imaging

options.label: Hypovitaminosis A
options.detail: Wrong syndrome entirely

options.label: Traumatic femoral fractures
options.detail: Bilateral, symmetrical, folding fractures in demineralised bone are not traumatic

options.label: Spinal trauma
options.detail: The kyphosis is part of generalised bone disease

stages.explanation: The treatment is calcium — parenteral first, then oral — with a correct thermal gradient, a new UVB source measured with a meter rather than assumed, dusted insects and cage rest. Naming the fractures in the diagnosis is what protects the animal from being handled normally while its bones are still soft.
